entry.title: Dinard Beach
entry.summary: The main beach of Dinard is a long sandy bay below Belle Epoque villas on the Emerald Coast of Brittany. The tide range is large, and the beach has striped cabins, lifeguards in season and a seafront promenade.

entry.title: Plage de la Salis
entry.summary: A sheltered sandy beach at Antibes with calm, shallow water that suits families, and views across the bay. Public sections sit alongside private beach restaurants.

entry.title: Plage de la Croisette
entry.summary: The sandy beaches along the famous Boulevard de la Croisette in Cannes, a mix of private beach clubs and free public sections. The water is calm and shallow, and the promenade is ideal for a stroll with views of the bay.

entry.title: Podgora Beach
entry.summary: A long pebble beach in Podgora on the Makarska Riviera, backed by pines with views across to the island of Brac. It is quieter than Makarska and Brela, and the water is clear.

entry.title: Medulin Beach
entry.summary: A broad bay at the southern tip of Istria with shallow water, pebble and stone beaches and pine shade. It is a family favourite, and several beaches along the coast have showers and lifeguards in season.

entry.title: Girandella Beach
entry.summary: A pebble beach in the resort of Rabac on the east coast of Istria, lined with pines and facing the Kvarner Bay. The water is clear, and there are sunbeds and cafes along the promenade.

entry.title: Jagodna Beach
entry.summary: A pebble beach in a clear bay on the south coast of Hvar, east of Hvar Town, backed by pine forest. It is quieter than the town beaches, and the water is clear and sheltered.

entry.title: Praia do Carvoeiro
entry.summary: A small golden beach set in a cove below the whitewashed village of Carvoeiro, with cliffs on each side. It sits in the heart of the village, so cafes, restaurants and shops are a few steps away.

entry.title: Praia da Costa Nova
entry.summary: A long Atlantic beach beside the colourful striped houses of Costa Nova near Aveiro, with wide golden sand and dunes. It has a relaxed village feel, with seafood restaurants and boardwalks.

entry.title: Praia dos Pescadores
entry.summary: The central beach of Albufeira, reached through a tunnel from the old town, with golden sand and cliffs on both sides. It is popular and lively, with restaurants and bars close by.

entry.title: Praia de Ofir
entry.summary: A long Atlantic beach in the Esposende area of northern Portugal, backed by dunes and pine woods. The surf is strong, and the area is known for windsurfing and kitesurfing and its relaxed pace.

entry.title: Sitges Beach
entry.summary: A calm golden town beach in Sitges, with the baroque church of Sant Bartomeu and Santa Tecla on the headland. It is close to the old town and has showers, lifeguards in season and plenty of cafes nearby.

entry.title: Playa de la Malvarrosa
entry.summary: The best-known city beach of Valencia, a wide stretch of fine sand backed by a palm-lined promenade. It is known for the paella restaurants along the front and is easy to reach from the centre by tram.

entry.title: Playa de San Lorenzo
entry.summary: A long, curved city beach in Gijon on the Asturian coast, backed by a promenade and the old fishermen quarter. The tide changes the beach greatly, and it is popular for surf lessons and sunset walks.

entry.title: Playa de Levante
entry.summary: The main sandy beach of Benidorm, curving along the east side of the old town beneath a high-rise skyline. It is wide, well maintained and equipped with showers, lifeguards and a long promenade.

entry.title: Cala Benirras
entry.summary: A sheltered cove on the north coast of Ibiza with a small beach of sand and pebbles, framed by pine-covered hills and the Cap Bernat rock stack. It is known for informal drumming at sunset on Sundays.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Rimini
entry.summary: A very wide sandy beach on the Adriatic coast, backed by a long promenade and a large number of bathing establishments. The water is shallow and warm, which makes it popular with families and young groups.

entry.title: Lido di Camaiore
entry.summary: A long sandy stretch on the Tuscan Versilia coast, lined with bathing establishments and a short pier. Pine woods and the Apuan Alps frame the beach, and the area suits families.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Serapo
entry.summary: A broad crescent of fine sand beside the old town of Gaeta, backed by a promenade and Monte Orlando. The water is shallow near the shore, and the beach has plenty of lidos.

entry.title: Baia dei Turchi
entry.summary: A natural bay in Salento, a few kilometres north of Otranto, with fine pale sand, pines and clear shallow water. It lies in a protected area and is one of the more natural beaches on this coast.

entry.title: Cala Cipolla
entry.summary: A pretty bay on the south coast of Sardinia near Chia, with soft sand, clear water and a rocky headland. It is quieter than the better-known Chia beaches and feels wild and open.

entry.title: Falasarna Beach
entry.summary: A broad golden beach on the far west coast of Crete, with clear turquoise water and views toward the Gramvousa peninsula. It is known for its sunsets and has room for everyone even in summer.

entry.title: Tsilivi Beach
entry.summary: A long sandy beach north of Zakynthos Town with gently shelving, warm water and a lively strip of beach bars and tavernas. It offers a wide choice of water sports and suits families.

entry.title: Anthony Quinn Bay
entry.summary: A small, sheltered bay of clear turquoise water enclosed by pine-covered rocks near Faliraki on Rhodes. It is named after the actor Anthony Quinn and is popular for swimming and snorkelling.

entry.title: Paradise Beach
entry.summary: A long sandy bay on the south coast of Mykonos, known for its beach clubs and lively atmosphere from morning to night. The water is clear and the sand is golden, with bars and water sports along the shore.

entry.title: Cap Ferret Ocean Beach
entry.summary: Wild Atlantic beaches and high dunes at the tip of the Cap Ferret peninsula, facing the Banc dArguin. Swimming is best at the supervised beaches, since waves and rips are strong.

entry.title: Plage d'Argent
entry.summary: A long, silvery-white beach on Porquerolles, the largest of the Iles dHyeres, within a national park and without cars. Pine forest and warm clear water make it feel like the tropics.

entry.title: Hossegor Lake Beach
entry.summary: A calm sandy beach on the lake of Hossegor, ringed by pines and villas, offering a gentler alternative to the surf on the nearby ocean beaches. It has lifeguards in summer and is good for small children.

entry.title: Lacanau Ocean Beach
entry.summary: A broad sandy Atlantic beach backed by dunes and pines, with strong waves that have made Lacanau one of France best-known surf spots. The central beach is lively, and the southern sections are quieter.

entry.title: Zaton Beach
entry.summary: A long, shallow beach between Zadar and Nin on the Adriatic, mostly sand with pebbles in places. A flat shoreline and warm water make it popular with families.
